lede: Two landmark consumer studies drop within 48 hours — BCG/Altagamma and the luxury market's AI maturity gap — while agentic ad infrastructure gets its open-standards backbone, and a fashion AI content platform signals the industrialisation of luxury creative production.

stories.headline: BCG × Altagamma: 87% of Luxury Consumers Use AI Weekly — But 57% of Houses Are Still AI Laggards
stories.summary: The 12th edition of BCG and Altagamma's True-Luxury Global Consumer Insights — drawing on 10,000+ respondents across 11 markets — finds that 87% of luxury consumers now use AI or GenAI tools weekly and 79% deploy LLMs specifically for luxury research, comparing leather goods, watches, and hospitality. Despite this, BCG separately estimates that 57% of luxury companies remain at emerging or stagnating levels of AI maturity. The report projects 2–5% market growth for FY26, accelerating to 4–7% by 2029, with AI-enabled personalisation and retention of top-tier clients identified as the key value levers.

stories.headline: Adform Joins IAB Tech Lab to Operationalise AAMP 2.0 — The Open Infrastructure Layer for Agentic Advertising Is Taking Shape
stories.summary: Adform announced on 8 July its deepened collaboration with IAB Tech Lab to operationalise AAMP 2.0 (Agentic Advertising Management Protocols), the emerging open-standards framework that extends OpenRTB, AdCOM, and VAST into autonomous, machine-speed ad transactions. Adform has already opened 800+ capabilities in its FLOW platform via Model Context Protocol, enabling external AI agents to plan, buy, and optimise across the full advertising lifecycle. The announcement raises a direct board-level question for luxury media buyers: will your agency's agentic infrastructure be interoperable with the emerging standard, or will proprietary fragmentation erode the transparency luxury brands now demand?

stories.headline: 57% of Luxury Companies Are AI Laggards as Consumer Adoption Races Ahead — BCG's Maturity Verdict Is a Wake-Up Call
stories.summary: Luxury consumers are now more AI-fluent than the brands selling to them: 79% use LLMs to research luxury purchases, and AI tools are now trusted by 29% of respondents — almost on par with word of mouth, and more than twice as trusted as social media or influencers. BCG's companion analysis of 1,000 companies confirms 57% of luxury sector firms sit at 'emerging or stagnating' AI maturity levels. The implication for LVMH's data and media teams is direct: AI is not the future discovery channel — it is today's, and the competitive gap will compound.

stories.headline: Pixel Moda Produces 14 Million AI-Assisted Pictures and Videos a Year for 900+ Luxury Brands — Industrial-Scale Creative Is Now the Norm
stories.summary: Business of Fashion spotlights Pixel Moda, the global e-commerce media producer that generates 14 million pictures and videos annually for over 900 luxury brands, retailers, and multi-brand platforms using a blend of AI-generated and AI-assisted production. The platform supported Etro's AI-driven content overhaul — presented at BoF VOICES in December 2025 — which resulted in a 46% growth in e-commerce revenue over twelve months while preserving brand identity. The case makes the strongest available argument that AI creative scale is now a direct revenue driver, not just a cost line.

stories.headline: Luxury Market Enters New Growth Cycle — AI Disruption of Purchase Funnels Identified as One of Four Structural Forces Reshaping the Sector
stories.summary: Bain's spring update of its Luxury Goods Worldwide Market Study — released today via its Media Center — frames 2026 as a stabilisation year (€1,440–€1,470B total luxury spending, 0–2% growth at constant rates) shaped by four interconnected forces, explicitly naming AI's rapid reshuffling of go-to-customer funnels as a structural shift alongside experience-over-ownership trends and geographic rebalancing. The Americas are leading personal luxury recovery, driven by new-money US consumers from the AI and tech sectors. For LVMH's media and data teams, the report provides the macroeconomic framework justifying accelerated GEO and agentic commerce investment in H2.
